Level 3 shows how much [wind and solar capacity is being built](../daten/index.qmd). Whether it works shows up here: in the CO₂ emissions per kilowatt-hour of electricity generated.

| 2023 | 379 | 531 |

| 2025 | 344 (estimated) | not yet published |

## Emissions avoided by renewable energy

For Germany, the German Environment Agency calculates each year how many emissions renewables avoid: **265 Mt CO₂-equivalent in 2025**, about **78 % of it in the power sector** [@uba_vermiedene_2026].

There is no comparable official calculation for China, so this site does not estimate one.

## What to bear in mind when comparing

::: {.einordnung}
**Similar, not identical.** Both series measure direct CO₂ emissions per kilowatt-hour without upstream chains. The German figure refers to electricity generated in Germany and available for final consumption. China's factor is the official average factor for location-based accounting (e.g. in corporate GHG inventories).

**Model, not measurement.** "Avoided emissions" are a model calculation: they assume which fossil power plants would have generated electricity without renewables. They cannot be measured directly.

**Time lag.** China publishes its factors about two years later; the 2023 value appeared at the end of 2025.

**Why the German value rose in 2021–2022:** more coal was burned in those years – with weak wind in 2021 and as a substitute for natural gas during the 2022 energy crisis.
:::
